contact.note: ASSUMED as in the IKV trace: blade/skate-puck collisions keep half the approach speed (frictionless); boards and posts inelastic.

rw_return.note: after the pass the right wing goes back to the pose the cleaned track reads just after the goal (model readings), in a designed smootherstep move

limitations: PROPOSED rebuild from one broadcast camera; nothing is measured on the table.

Puck: hand readings of the broadcast frames (shots/edwall/puck-readings.json), back-projected to z = 6 mm; motion-blurred streak frames weigh less; readings near the near board are biased toward +y because the board's top edge hides the ice, so the rest position is snapped to the board.
No newer puck detector track was available on the remote (no claude/puck-detector-* branch at build time); this trace uses the hand readings above.

Right wing (passer) and centre (shooter): the lunges and turns are DESIGNED smootherstep moves fitted to the puck readings and the goal; the cleaned figure tracks are interpolated through these fast moves and only fix the rest poses and the return.

Both plays are modelled as heel-groove carries: the puck stays at the touching point of the stick heel from catch to release and leaves with that point's velocity (NTHF: 'carries the puck with the heel groove'). slide_check.carries reports whether the needed force stays inside the contact-normal fan of the groove.

The centre's shovel and the goal are hidden in the broadcast (behind the E goalie and the near goal frame): the shot is DESIGNED to score into the open far (+y) corner; its exact contact and line are not observed.
The other ten figures follow the cleaned model tracks (data/games/nm26-semifinal/g2/figure-tracks-smooth.json, PROPOSED, not verified frame by frame).
Ice friction 926.1 mm/s^2 is borrowed from the spjass slide fit; figure restitution 0.5 frictionless; puck thickness 12 mm assumed.

fitted.method: two stages (scripts/edwall-trace.py --fit pass|shot), each a differential-evolution search inside fit.bounds and a Nelder-Mead polish: pass = the passer's rest rotation, lunge and turn against the puck readings (streak weight 0.15) and the slide-rule limits; shot = the shooter's lunge and turns against the goal window, the goal-line target and the slide-rule limits
